title: BTS FESTA 2026 Day 7: 'Normal Log' Released + Three Song Re-Releases (JK, RM, Jimin)
detail: June 7, 2026 — BTS FESTA 2026 resumes following the Memorial Day content pause with a multi-item content drop on Weverse and Bangtan TV YouTube. Big Hit Music releases the 'Normal Log' — a behind-the-scenes vlog-style video offering ARMY a candid look at the group's recent activities during the ARIRANG World Tour and FESTA preparations, consistent with the casual, fan-facing format of previous FESTA logs. Alongside the Normal Log, three classic BTS songs with deep fan emotional resonance are re-released and newly promoted on streaming platforms: 'Never Let Go' (Jungkook) — originally released in June 2024 as an anniversary track for ARMY, re-released on YouTube and Spotify to coincide with the approaching 13th anniversary; 'Bicycle' (RM) — RM's fan-favorite solo track from 2021, re-uploaded to YouTube, SoundCloud, and Spotify as part of the FESTA programming; and 'Dear. ARMY' live clip featuring Jimin — a live performance clip from 2023 capturing Jimin's direct message to the fanbase, re-released on YouTube. All three re-releases are intentionally selected to resonate with ARMY during the emotional final week of pre-anniversary buildup, with each track carrying strong lyrical associations with the BTS–ARMY bond. The combined releases trend on social media in multiple regions. Busan Asiad Main Stadium anniversary concerts are now 5 days away (June 12–13).

media.caption: BTS FESTA 2026 Day 7: 'Normal Log' released alongside re-releases of 'Never Let Go' (JK), 'Bicycle' (RM), and 'Dear. ARMY' (Jimin).

title: 'SWIM' Ties 'Dynamite' — 8th Consecutive Week at No. 1 on Billboard Global (Excl. US)
detail: June 7, 2026 (chart date June 6): BTS's 'SWIM' completes its 8th consecutive week at No. 1 on the Billboard Global (Excl. US) chart, officially tying 'Dynamite' (2020) for BTS's longest-ever run at the top of that chart. The milestone is significant: 'Dynamite' held the No. 1 spot for 8 consecutive weeks in late 2020 and became the song that cemented BTS's global superstar status. Matching that record with 'SWIM' — the lead single from their 2026 comeback album ARIRANG — signals that the post-military reunion momentum has sustained at an extraordinary level for nearly two months since ARIRANG's March release. On the companion Billboard Global 200, 'SWIM' rises from No. 10 to No. 4, showing renewed momentum likely tied to increased streaming activity ahead of the June 12–13 Busan anniversary concerts. BTS now holds the record for the most No. 1 leaders on the Billboard Global (Excl. US) chart at 8 — double the nearest competitors (Bad Bunny, BLACKPINK, and Taylor Swift each with 4). All 13 ARIRANG vocal tracks remain active on global charts simultaneously, marking the 10th straight week of that feat. The 8-week No. 1 run for 'SWIM' represents an era-defining commercial achievement in BTS's reunion chapter.

media.caption: 'SWIM' ties 'Dynamite' with 8 consecutive weeks at No. 1 on Billboard Global (Excl. US) — chart dated June 6, 2026.
